title: Method for the differentiation of radiation-induced photocurrent from total measured current in P3HT/PCBM BHJ photodiodes
author: Hupman, Valitova, et al.
materials: Initially, to measure the current coming from the device, triaxial cables were used which had alligator clips at the end to connect to contact pads on the edge of the substrate. To decrease the Compton current, the bulky alligator clips needed to be placed outside of the irradiation field. To accomplish this a 3-D printed holder was used with pogo pins to contact the photodiode (Fig. 2). Next, wires were soldered to the ends of the pogo pins and brought outside of the beam. This reduced the size of the contacts in the beam. Furthermore, the 3-D printed holder allowed for easy device alignment within the beam and the path of the wires could be more easily reproduced when changing from a BHJ diode to a PS device. An added benefit of the 3-D printed holder is that it makes it easy to shield the BHJ photodiode from light.Fig. 2Picture of the device holder with and without the top to allow easy electrical contact. The holder shields light from reaching the photodiode and allows easy and consistent contact on the devices.Fig. 2

A BHJ photodiode was irradaited and the current measured on the ITO electrode using an SMU (Keithley 2614B, Tektronix Inc., Beaverton, USA) as depicted in Fig. 3. Two distinct currents are labelled that contribute to the measured current. First, there is the current induced inside the BHJ semiconductors Idet which is analogous to photocurrent generated when a light is incident on a photodiode. Second, there is a Compton current Irad,ITO which is generated in the electrodes, contacts, and wires associated with the ITO electrode due to the incident radiation beam and the associated secondary electrons impinging upon them. A similar current, Irad,Al, is generated in the top-contact electrode and associated conductors. When a megavoltage photon beam (of the type encountered in a radiation therapy setting) interacts in a water-like material it creates electrons primarily via Compton scatter and some photoelectric effect. These electrons have enough energy to produce additional excitations and ionizations. The net result is a shower of electrons spanning a large range of energies. Electrons interacting in the electric contacts and wires can produce a current that contributes to the measured current represented by Irad,[ITO/Al] in the figure. The Compton current produced in the aluminum contact and wires Irad,Al does not contribute to the current measured on the ITO electrode. However, if the SMU were connected to measure the current coming from the aluminum electrode Irad,Al will contribute to the current and Irad,ITO will not. Furthermore, the magnitude of Idet will be the same, but it will be the opposite direction. In equation form these measurements can be represented by:ISMU,ITO,BHJ = -Idet + Irad,ITOISMU,Al,BHJ = Idet + Irad,AlFig. 3Schematic showing the two circuits used for the correction method. On the left the bulk heterojunction (BHJ) diode is placed in the radiation beam and the current is measured with an SMU connected to the ITO electrode. This measurement has current induced in the detector (Idet) and Compton current induced in the electrodes and wires (Irad,ITO). On the right a polystyrene device has been placed in the irradiation beam in place of the BHJ diode and the current measured coming from the ITO electrode. The PS device will have no detector current (Idet), but will measure a Compton current (Irad,ITO). To calculate the detector current (Idet) the current measured with the PS setup is subtracted from the BHJ diode setup.Fig. 3

To correct for the Irad,[ITO/Al] current and obtain the detector current Idet we fabricated devices with polystrene (PS) instead of the BHJ. We expect that excitons will be generated in the PS layer just like the BHJ. However, given the insulating nature of PS, and the absence of a donor/acceptor interface, we do not expect any significant detector current. The measured current will be dominated by the extraneous contributions. Furthermore, if the irradiation setup is the same as when irradiating the BHJ (same beam energy, dose rate, etc.) then the Irad,[ITO/Al] current should be the same as measured for the BHJ. By measuring this current and subtracting it from the current measured with the BHJ measured current we can calculate the Idet current with the ITO electrode using:ISMU,ITO,BHJ - ISMU,ITO,PS = (-Idet + Irad,ITO) - (Irad,ITO)ISMU,ITO,BHJ - ISMU,ITO,PS = -Idet

steps.title: Assemble 3‑D printed holder and contacts
steps.instruction: Print the device holder, attach pogo pins to contact the photodiode, solder wires to the pogo pins, and route the wires outside the irradiation field; the holder also shields ambient light from the BHJ device.

substeps.instruction: Print the holder (Fig. 2) designed to hold the photodiode and accommodate pogo pins.
Insert pogo pins into the holder so they will contact the ITO and Al electrodes when the device is placed.
Solder a wire to each pogo pin and guide the wires so they exit the holder and lie completely outside the radiation beam.
Place the holder (with or without its top) onto the BHJ/PS device to make electrical contact while keeping the contacts and wires out of the beam.
Confirm that the holder blocks external light from reaching the photodiode.

steps.title: Connect SMU to ITO electrode
steps.instruction: Attach the Keithley 2614B source‑measure unit (SMU) to the ITO electrode via the soldered wires and set the SMU to measure current.

substeps.instruction: Connect the SMU leads to the wires coming from the ITO pogo pin.
Configure the SMU (Keithley 2614B, Tektronix Inc., Beaverton, USA) for low‑current measurement (pA range).

steps.title: Measure BHJ current on ITO
steps.instruction: Place the BHJ photodiode (P3HT/PCBM) in the megavoltage photon beam and record the current reported by the SMU (I_SMU,ITO,BHJ).

substeps.instruction: Insert the BHJ device into the irradiation field using the holder.
Ensure beam parameters (energy, dose rate) are identical to those used for later PS measurements.
Read and record the SMU current value (I_SMU,ITO,BHJ), which equals –I_det + I_rad,ITO.

steps.title: Measure BHJ current on Al electrode
steps.instruction: Reconnect the SMU to the aluminum (top‑contact) electrode and record I_SMU,Al,BHJ under the same irradiation conditions.

substeps.instruction: Switch the SMU leads to the Al pogo pin.
Read and record the SMU current value (I_SMU,Al,BHJ), which equals I_det + I_rad,Al.

steps.title: Measure PS reference current on ITO
steps.instruction: Replace the BHJ device with a polystyrene (PS) device of identical geometry, keep all wiring unchanged, irradiate, and record I_SMU,ITO,PS.

substeps.instruction: Remove the BHJ photodiode from the holder and insert the PS device.
Maintain the same beam energy, dose rate, and field size as for the BHJ measurement.
Read and record the SMU current (I_SMU,ITO,PS), which equals I_rad,ITO (no detector current).

steps.title: Measure PS reference current on Al electrode
steps.instruction: Connect the SMU to the Al electrode of the PS device and record I_SMU,Al,PS under identical beam conditions.

substeps.instruction: Switch the SMU leads to the Al pogo pin.
Read and record the SMU current (I_SMU,Al,PS), which equals I_rad,Al.

steps.title: Calculate detector current (Idet)
steps.instruction: Subtract the PS reference current from the BHJ current for each electrode to obtain the true detector current.

substeps.instruction: Compute Idet (ITO) = –(I_SMU,ITO,BHJ – I_SMU,ITO,PS).
Compute Idet (Al) = I_SMU,Al,BHJ – I_SMU,Al,PS.
Verify that the two Idet values have opposite sign but equal magnitude, confirming the correction.

steps.title: Optional simultaneous dual‑electrode check
steps.instruction: Measure both ITO and Al currents at the same time and compare the two independently calculated Idet values for consistency.

steps.title: Validate method across field sizes
steps.instruction: Repeat the BHJ and PS measurements for multiple radiation field sizes (3 × 3 cm², 10 × 10 cm², 20 × 20 cm²) and compare corrected currents to a commercial ionization chamber.

substeps.instruction: For each field size, record I_SMU,ITO,BHJ, I_SMU,ITO,PS, I_SMU,Al,BHJ, and I_SMU,Al,PS.
Calculate corrected Idet for each size using the subtraction formulas.
Plot total BHJ current, PS current, and corrected Idet versus field size (as in Fig. 4).
Determine the percentage of total signal due to Compton current: (I_PS / I_BHJ) × 100 % (e.g., 11 ± 3 % for 3 × 3 cm², >60 % for 20 × 20 cm²).
Measure background with no device (alligator clips in beam) – 200 ± 50 pA for a 10 × 10 cm² field.
Compare the corrected Idet output factors (signal normalized to 10 × 10 cm²) with those from a commercial ion chamber (Fig. 6) to confirm agreement.
